page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 24 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with Passmark memory scores and large-block read-only (210.08 GB/sec) and write (98.02 GB/sec) memory bandwidth tests ranking in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression also demonstrates strong performance at 31.99 GB/sec. Most general compute benchmarks, including Geekbench single-core (1580.0) and multi-core (13676.0) scores, fall within the average range. However, software compilation with clang is a notable strength, scoring 39257.0. Conversely, the instance exhibits weak to poor performance in LLM text generation, with the 135M model achieving 40.51 tokens/sec and the 7B model dropping to 7.8 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x2iezn.metal instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, trading off local storage and GPU acceleration for massive RAM capacity and high-speed network throughput. This profile makes it suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, memory-intensive data processing, and software compilation pipelines. It is less suitable for workloads requiring local high-speed NVMe storage or real-time LLM text generation.
